one_sentence_story: In 1964–1965 in Córdoba, Yale physiologist José Delgado halted a charging bull mid-sprint with a handheld radio 'stimoceiver' — landing on Page 1 of The New York Times, though later analysis proved his caudate-nucleus pulse forced a basal-ganglia motor turn rather than erasing anger, while his wireless hardware paved the way for modern Parkinson's Deep Brain Stimulation.
so_what_for_you: Whenever headlines hype 'mind-control brain chips,' apply the Córdoba filter: separate real medical neuromodulation of motor/rhythm circuits (like Parkinson's DBS) from exaggerated claims of controlling complex human thoughts.
